spans.text: ...Inside the bar at Stasi HQ, Wiesbaden District.
The server bows respectfully and leads the guests into a secluded box.
Two non-alcoholic Negronis, please.
Yes, ma'am.
The server soon returns with two glasses filled with pink liquid. After putting down the drinks, he leaves the box in silence.
Now that they will no longer be disturbed, Romy picks up her glass and gives it a swirl.
I hope my order is to your taste, Colonel Felix.
Non-alcoholic Negroni. Exactly what I'd expect you to order, Frau Romy.
You did say once that you like to keep your work and recreation separate, and that you don't drink on the job.
So I'm still on the job right now?
I'm guessing you don't like any of the bars in the Wiesbaden District.
Especially one so close to the White Zone.
This is practically a staff's canteen.
Since we're having a meeting at what's basically a workplace, we're on the job.
But at your rank, are you ever NOT on the job?
You're just like General Riefenstahl—so thoughtful and always on top of things. Speaking of which, how has the general been doing lately?
My father is in pretty good shape. He's taken to going on walks and fishing since he retired. Apart from some old injuries, he's doing great.
That's very good to hear. With a daughter like you, I'm sure the general has nothing much to worry about.
What about you, Colonel? Is there anything that troubles you?
I just have to keep the Hugo Eberlein Guard Regiment in check. Other than that, there's nothing else for me to worry about.
No wonder they say, General Schweinsteiger is the foundation, and you and the sturdiest chunk of granite on that foundation.
The Eberlein Guard Regiment remain loyal to the Socialist Unity Party and we accept the leadership of every party chairman.
I suppose I'm not the first to have heard this.
You're obviously not the first to have asked me that question, nor will you be the last.
And no matter who comes asking, my answer will always be the same.
Even if the party falls apart?
...Frau Romy, what I'm about to say may sound a bit blunt, but I speak from the heart.
I am a natural-born soldier, not a natural-born politician.
When the party is in disarray, the Eberlein Guard Regiment is the best holy sword.
When the party falls apart, we are the empty crown.
You promised General Riefenstahl that you would no longer get involved in military affairs after entering the civil service.
I am still keeping this promise.
Right now you're talking to Romy Riefenstahl, Director of the Ministry for State Security, not the daughter of Heinz Riefenstahl.
Now, what I want to discuss with you is not just the affairs of the SED.
It has become a national issue concerning the German Democratic Republic itself.
Regarding the progress of the URNC... I think you and I are both clear that no one can stop history from unfolding.
Just like slavery, no matter how prominent it once was, it is destined to be left behind in the march of history.
...I have the right to remain silent on this matter.
You should understand that if we join this melee, it won't bring clarity to the situation—only further escalation and destruction.
War is in your interest; for you, it is a bargaining chip.
But for us, war is only about advancing and death.
We cannot stop the war, so we retain the right to sheathe our swords.
I am not a fanatical warmonger.
But you have a strong thirst for power.
...Someone with no desire for power wouldn't be the commander of the Hugo Eberlein Guard Regiment.
You seem to be implying that you were forced into this position.
But in fact, you know full well that sometimes when you're put in a certain position, the best thing to do is to accumulate enough strength and power to be worthy of that position.
It is a cliff with no way down. Either you climb, or you die.
Sorry, I'm not a bureaucrat—I don't have the gift of eloquence for negotiations.
Felix drains the content of his glass, then he turns the vessel upside down to show that he hasn't left a single drop.
Looks like I've finished my drink.
Felix rises to his feet and bows slightly in apology.
Whoosh—the frame around the large oil painting hanging on the wall behind him suddenly lights up. With a soft mechanical hum, the frame swings off the wall.
Felix slowly pulls the frame all the way open, revealing an intricately constructed room. A man is sitting inside, drinking on his own.
Secretary Groß?!
Felix slowly returns to his seat. The man in the hidden chamber stands up and walks over to join them with a smile.
Romy makes her way to the entrance of the box and gestures toward the server in the distance.
Three Negronis, please.
Three glasses of pink liquid smelling strongly of alcohol are soon served.
Romy picks up her glass with a smile.
What's the rush, Colonel Felix...?
I believe we're just getting started.
...Romy's office.
Hoffman checks if all relevant personnel has received and read the notice.
Across the table, Q is leisurely sipping her coffee.
The justifications, specific measures, and inspection methods for strengthening the security within the White Zone are all clearly stated.
Even the template and procedure for bilateral reporting of the new measures are highlighted.
As expected of Herr Hoffmann.
In the past, we only needed to report the access list to the garrison, but there were still plenty of screw-ups. Now we need to report to both the Stasi and the garrison at the same time.
I can't imagine how many mistakes there will be. You can't be too meticulous.
What about you? Any progress on your end?
Hard to say.
If your job is to publish a chemistry textbook, then my job is to get students to break down stable salt into sodium ions.
...You could consider using some catalysts.
Believe me, I've been pouring the stuff in already, but I worked too closely with them in the past. It's kinda difficult to get dirt on them without showing up as a turncoat witness, you know?
That's why this task was given to you.
Q puts down her coffee and sits up straight.
So you really haven't heard anything about Project Valkyrie?
Has it really been scrubbed clean?
...All we know from public knowledge is that it's related to the wife and daughter of Oberstein, the incumbent Minister of Industry and Information Technology, Vice-President of the State Council.
As for the specific report, you can read it for yourself.
Practically everyone who knows anything about this has gone to Antarctica with the Relics Agency. The information we have could be entirely false.
Sometimes, what we need isn't factual information.
But useful information.
...Thanks for the tip.
After tidying up the documents scattered all over her desk, Q gets up to leave.
What about J's disappearance? Is it really no big deal?
...Since no body has been found, someone will eventually come knocking.
Don't worry, getting rid of bodies has always been a complicated craft.
...Do you think he may have gone back to his hometown? I've been hearing him muttering something about selling pork knuckles back at home.
...Herr Hoffmann, thank you for making me laugh for three seconds straight even as I get crushed under a mountain of work.
...In the temporary command room.
Click. A call request from an encrypted comms channel.
Commander, it's the Earl.
After keeping the communicator on hold for a few more seconds, the Commander nods and gestures for the call to be answered.
Earl.
I believe the last time we spoke, we still had an ideal mentor-mentee relationship.
...I once had a lot of respect for you.
Respect—which implies looking up to me.
Now you have matured to a point where we can speak on equal terms.
You have met whom you wanted to.
I'm not getting in touch because I need you—quite the contrary.
Right now, you need me.
I hope ambitious young people can walk a bright and promising path—
not rush into the White Zone and spark a violent commotion.
Your current situation is no better than when you were trapped in the Black Zone—if anything, it's worse.
But even so, I'm still willing to offer you help, just as I did in Avernus.
It's good for young people to have their own ideas.
I know you don't agree with some of my decisions, but I've already made significant concessions.
I know I shouldn't try to keep an eagle bound under my protection.
I only need to wait—wait for the day when the weary bird returns to its nest.
...And you believe the time has come.
There are no eternal enemies, Commander.
Only eternal interests.
What we went through was merely a small, internal conflict.
It wasn't fatal. Our interests are bound together, and our positions are aligned.
No matter what happens, G&K stands behind you.
That holds true for you, for Kryuger, and for me.
...Then what's the plan this time?
I sent you from the Neo-Soviet Union to Berlin because of Morridow.
Yes, and this mission has revealed to me a glimpse of the real world.
Young people are always so full of curiosity.
Will you tell me the truth?
No, you must unearth it and find out for yourself. That way, you will find it easier to accept.
If you wish to find out William's true identity and what he intends to do...
You must first get to the bottom of one thing—Project Valkyrie.
...Maybe I don't even care about the whys and the whats anymore. I just think he needs to pay for everything he's done.
The choice is ultimately yours.
If you want to learn the truth, investigating this is the only way.
If you want to eliminate him, then I can offer you one last bit of help.
Romy and I aren't exactly close, but the Stasi has already taken one step towards us.
Given your current situation, it would benefit you greatly if you could secure the Stasi's cooperation.
Thank you, Earl.
Finally, some genuine words from you.
Click. The Earl terminates the call.
After pondering for a moment in silence, the Commander turns to AR-18.
If you're asking for my opinion...
I think you need more information.
To take on an enemy, you must have a comprehensive understanding of him.
...But this is most certainly a trap.
He would never have contacted me if this wouldn't benefit him in some way.
Perhaps you should think of it from another perspective.
Instead of worrying about how this would benefit him, consider what you want to accomplish and whether this would help.
What do I want to accomplish?
The Commander unconsciously drums their fingers on the desk. The chaotic rhythm betrays their unease.
In the very beginning, all I wanted to do was to expel Sangvis Ferri forces so that the Griffin base could operate in a safe and stable environment.
Then I wanted to save the AR Team. I wanted to save Machlian. I wanted to save Ange...

But now, even I don't know what I want to accomplish. I seem to have been stuck in a quagmire for so long, I no longer remember the days before I stepped into it, and I can't recall where I'm supposed to be headed.
I've led one operation after another, always thinking that the next one would finally reveal the whole truth.
But with each answer, new mysteries emerge—an endless cycle, as if they'll never be solved.
I understand how exhausting it must feel, Commander.
But hesitation and doubt are the last things you can afford on the battlefield. Now is not the time to waver.
I know...
...Maybe I'm just feeling fearful because I'm hitting closer and closer to home.
I know the truth is about to be uncovered, yet somehow, I've started to feel afraid.
AR-18 walks up to the Commander and points at the monitor in front of them.
You have so many shoulders to lean on—don't carry all the weight alone.
These shoulders that I can lean on are also weaknesses that can be exploited.
You should think more of yourself.
You're right. Rather than worrying about others, I really should focus more on myself.
What am I really after on this trip to Germany?
Who am I fighting for? What am I fighting for?
It may take you a lifetime to find the answers.
Indeed...
The Commander gets to their feet and pats their own tired cheeks.
I may feel lost and conflicted, but I will not stop moving forward...
AR-18, escort me to Nele's residence.
Yes, Commander.
...In Nele's rented flat.
J looks as fatigued as the Commander. They stare at each other in silence.
Finally remember you have to deal with me, eh, Commander?
How are you gonna do this then, Griffin's way or Statesec's way?
There's no need for this game of probing between us.
I'll cut straight to the chase—I need you to help me contact Ms. Romy.
...You think you've got the bargaining chip to negotiate with Romy?
You have no idea what you're dealing with.
And she isn't the only terrifying woman in the Stasi.
I would like to make a deal, not a declaration of war.
You're just an ordinary PMC commander.
Romy is backed by the Socialist Unity Party and the German Democratic Republic.
To put it plainly, the final boss that you want to fight—the mastermind behind Paradeus—is also part of the Socialist Unity Party.
No matter how confident you are in your plan, I urge you to just give up.
No...
When Ms. Romy handed Task Force DEFY's neural cores over to me, I knew... we would work together again.
...If I remember correctly, hadn't she already helped you back in Avernus?
Is it not clear enough? She can't openly antagonize him.
He is the Vice-Chairman of the Socialist Unity Party... someone who sits in the first three rows.
When I first saw Ms. Romy at Paradeus' underground plant that time, I could immediately tell that she is an ambitious person.
There's no way she'd be satisfied with her current position.
...That's why I want to take a gamble.
Have you gone mad?
This is what I must do for a small fry like me to survive at the table.
I am willing to bet that when it comes to dealing with Paradeus, Ms. Romy will take my side.
...You must have found out already back then... the Stasi was involved in those two production chains.
Which is why... I must speak to Ms. Romy directly.
Her path upward allows no room for mistakes, and this is the perfect time to clean up that mess properly.
The Commander tosses a communicator to J.
...I just hope you know what you're doing.
I've never been more clear-headed.
I have a plan—one that will not only allow you to return to the Stasi without issue, but also help you clean up the shady dealings between your people and Paradeus.
And most importantly... I'm going to cut off one of Paradeus' arms and sabotage Project Cocoon.
After a brief moment of hesitation, J raises the communicator.
I'm going on all in with you, even though I barely have anything left. You'd better be making the right call!
